Freezing fog rolled in off the Columbia near Wallula overnight, and every plane at the Pasco airport needs de-icing before the first flights. The lead wants volunteers at 4:30.

Coming in: your paycheck, side hustles, a partner's part-time paycheck, unemployment benefits for 6 months after a layoff (41% of your last job's pay, between $1,500 and $4,900 a month), and Social Security, a public pension and 401(k) payouts once you retire.
21 and over: drinks at The Little Kiss Pasta Bar, Grenache & Gather, The Royal Brick and Laughing Lad's taproom only show once you're 21.

🛡️ Insurance (Life tab, about $220 a month with the phone): full coverage ($130) or liability only ($55) on your vehicle, homeowners at about $95 for the fixer-upper and $140 for the farmhouse, renters insurance (renters) or a $500, $1,000 or $2,500 deductible (owners). Cheaper coverage saves a little every month, but crashes, deer, ditches, theft, break-ins, fires and storms then cost you more: full coverage pays vehicle losses after a $500 deductible, renters insurance pays for your things after $250, and a homeowners policy pays after your deductible. Owners can also take a cheaper wind and hail plan (about 0.15% of the home's value a year less): a windstorm claim then costs you up to 1% of what the house is worth instead of the regular deductible, and the sheet shows that in dollars.
After the flood, the city wants to build up the levee along the river, and it's asking for volunteers and donations.
On a tablet, a computer or a phone held sideways, Home shows two columns, with your job, home, ride and recent journal entries at the side.
Dayton is throwing a summer festival around its historic train depot.

Owners pay property tax to the county twice a year, in April and October (about 1% of the home's value a year), and can borrow against the house (up to half the equity, at a year's rate + 1 point, over 10 years). Selling pays off what's left.
The volunteer firefighters are flipping pancakes at the station to raise money for new gear.

Events and jobs: the bluegrass jam, Grenache Fest, music nights, the grill opening, the spring garden rush, a summer cookout and more. Local jobs include line cook, barista, grocery clerk, bank teller, reporter, trades apprentice, medical assistant and ag technician.

Pay after taxes (13% on a small paycheck up to 22% on a big one) and the gas to drive to work and back (half with a carpool, less on remote days, and a bus pass instead of gas if you ride the county bus). Union dues and any 401(k) savings come out of it too.
🧭 Planning ahead shows your Social Security and pension for retirement (in Lifetime games you can retire from 62). Tap 📅 Money outlook .

Life brings people and pets: a partner (date nights, a part-time paycheck, and happier weeks), kids (about $950 a month each until 18, $400 of it childcare, plus $200 more if you commute 20+ miles; under about $5,000 a month of household pay, Working Connections childcare caps your childcare at $115; they bring the most joy in weeks you Rest or Show up for town, and more community), a dog (or a barn cat, about half a dog's cheer for about $20 a month), even a seat on the town council once your community standing is 60 or higher. These mostly arrive through events, so say yes when it fits your life.
Every driveway in town has a table out this Saturday.

Remote job: with a bachelor's degree you can work fully remote for a Seattle company: city pay and no commute, a one-time $900 fiber install, but no coworkers, so community fades faster, and layoffs are common.

Offers: for hard-to-fill jobs (nurses, nursing assistants, imaging techs, truckers, linemen, wind and reactor techs, teachers, phlebotomists, the lab) you can take the offer, ask for 5% more (People skill helps) or ask for a $3,000 sign-on bonus that you pay back if you leave inside a year. Asking can lose the offer (1 in 10).
Big choices (moving, buying a vehicle, quitting) list what will change in cash, weekly costs and stats before you say yes.

🪪 Union jobs (rail yard, Hanford, nurses, paraeducators, corrections, teachers, electricians, linemen) take 1.5% dues, give a 1.5% step raise each January and half the layoff risk. Every few years there's a contract vote: take the 2% deal, or strike for a few weeks on 40% strike pay for a likely 6% raise.
Mr. Q's Smokehouse is throwing a summer cookout on Preston Avenue. Brisket, beans and a cornhole tournament.

Seasonal work: the Bluewood lift (December–March), harvest trucking (July–August) and the Forest Service crew (June–September) lay you off when the season ends and call you back when it returns, with no application. Pair a winter job with a summer one, or ride unemployment for a few months.

🦷 Dental (insurance sheet, $28 a month): yearly checkups are free, an emergency dentist costs less, and a cracked tooth costs $400 instead of $1,400. A yearly checkup makes a cracked tooth less likely either way.

🌦️ Weather (the Life tab's Ready for weather card): in a wildfire-smoke summer, outdoor crews work shorter days in July and August (10% less pay, half the wear on your body) unless you choose to push through, which risks a sick week. A box-fan air filter ($45 to build with the Handy skill, or $160 for a purifier) keeps smoke out of your health at home for that year. After a windstorm, roofers are booked for weeks: wait with a tarp (a little happiness each week, and rain can get under it), pay about 30% more to jump the line, or fix it yourself with the Handy skill. After the flood, owners of the fixer-upper can raise the furnace and water heater to cut later flood cleanup by 80%. In winter, Home has a toggle to clear the neighbor's walk every snow (a little health, a little community). With community 40 or more you can be your street's block captain : each windstorm or outage you run the plan for an evening and gain community.
A customer is yelling at you about something that isn't your fault.
For Celebration Days, Tonnage Coffee & Strings opens to everyone: coffee, music on the sidewalk and a view of the parade.
A red banner appears when happiness or health drops below 30, with a suggested focus to fix it.
Grenache & Gather is pouring grenache from all over the valley, with a guest chef in the kitchen.
The Tri-Cities puts on the biggest fireworks show around.
The beer garden at the fairgrounds needs volunteers to pour for the Celebration Days crowd.
A sunburned cyclist riding the Lewis & Clark route stops on Main Street and asks where to fill a water bottle.
The historical society opens its old house museum on Main Street for the summer: 1880s furniture, photos and a creaky staircase.

Taxes (federal income tax, Social Security and Medicare; Washington has no income tax) take 13% of a paycheck up to $3,500 a month, rising smoothly to 16% at $6,000, 20% at $8,000 and 22% from $9,000 (2027 dollars). Every job pays at least Washington's minimum wage, about $3,050 a month full time. Food and utilities run about $700 a month.
There's also an Android app (APK) and a Windows installer on the game's GitHub releases page: github.com/krazow/The-Burg/releases.
A 5K along the Columbia this Saturday.
After 30 years, a coworker is retiring.

In Lifetime games you can retire from age 62 (on the Jobs tab). Retirement pays Social Security, and your 401(k) pays out 4% a year until 73, then more each year like the IRS required-distribution table (about 5% at 80 and 8% at 90). Social Security and a pension are untaxed up to $3,000 a month; 401(k) withdrawals are taxed about 10%.

🌳 Legacy: when a Lifetime game ends and you had kids, you can keep playing as your grandkid (18, with a name like Ann Lee II that you can change), with half your net worth (up to $250,000 in 2027 dollars) and some of your standing in town.

Stories: some events unfold over weeks: fixing up the fixer-upper, a friend's food truck, a Little League season you coach (a losing streak, a comeback and the season party), and the flood that leads to a new levee (it only comes after high water that the town didn't sandbag with your help, and if it reaches your place you'll spend a few weeks drying out). What you choose at each step changes what comes next.

Titles: 85+ Legend of the Burg , 70+ Pillar of the Community , 55+ Solid Waitsburger , 40+ Getting By on Main Street , below that Tumbleweed . Your best score for each length is kept, and Relaxed and Hard scores are labeled and kept separately from Normal ones: tap 🏆 Your records on the title screen to see them by length and mode, with your challenges and this week's weekly challenge.
Friends are heading to Walla Walla tasting rooms on Saturday.
A coworker is raising money for a family in need.
It's the busiest week of the year at Dreamy Garden Center: tomato starts, hanging baskets and cookies by the register.
Underlined words explain themselves. Tap Take-home .

Town goals: each season the town has a goal you work toward with your focus: 🌸 Get Celebration Days ready (6 weeks of Show up for town), 🌾 Bring in the harvest (5 weeks of Work extra, Side hustle or Show up for town), 🍂 Stock the food bank before winter (5 weeks of Show up for town), ❄️ Holiday food drive and shoveling for neighbors (4 weeks of Show up for town or Get outside). Finish it before the season ends for a boost in community and happiness. Your progress shows above the focus buttons.
River shapes for the Columbia, Snake and Yakima come from Natural Earth (public domain). The Walla Walla and Touchet rivers and the roads are drawn by hand.
Little extras: a haircut or spa day at Rouge helps your job applications for 2 weeks, an ad in The Touchet Tattler raises side-hustle pay 15% for 8 weeks, and a woodworking class eases a rut.

Going out every week: rent or mortgage, food and utilities, insurance and phone (you choose the coverage), gas (commute plus errands), truck payments, dog care, date nights, kids, health care (your $130 share of the plan at work before 50, or Apple Health for $0 with no job or pay under $1,900; more from 50 and 65), late-life care, tuition and focus costs. The 📅 money outlook on the Life tab projects the next 13 weeks.

Apprenticeships (electrician, plumber, power lineman; trade certificate needed): you start at 50% of a journeyman's pay (60% as a lineman) and step up every year over about 8,000 hours (4 years; 3 for a lineman), then earn full pay. Leaving starts it over.
Ice on everything in the foothills, and the heifers are calving.

Making a long commute work: office jobs (insurance agent, courthouse clerk, professor, scientist) have 2 remote days a week, so you drive in only 3; the loan officer and lab administrator have 3. The mall in Kennewick is always hiring and gives 10% off Tri-Cities trip stops, and the Pasco food plant pays 30% overtime in the August–October harvest pack. With community 30 or more you can join a carpool on the Jobs tab: half the gas, the drive wears on you less, and you stay in the loop. A carpool goes with the job: when you change jobs you drive alone until you join one again. Side hustles follow the seasons (harvest work in summer, plowing snow in winter, yard work, fixing cars) and pay up to 60% more as you get good at them. After 6 months without a side hustle you slowly get rusty and that extra fades.

🧓 Dad's appointments (Lifetime, in your late 40s or 50s): your sister calls from Spokane. Split the drives with her (money), pay for a driver and helper (more money), or take every drive yourself (happiness and health). With a job you can take Washington's paid family leave : up to 12 weeks at 90% of your pay (up to a cap), with your job's wear paused. While you're helping, a 🌿 respite weekend at the adult day program in Walla Walla gives back health and happiness caregiving took, never more.

🧭 Planning ahead (Life tab): the 📅 money outlook shows your next 13 weeks of pay and bills, the big ones (vehicle tabs, tuition, a lease renewal, a winter away) and the week, if any, your cash would dip below zero. It's also under the week's details.

Physical therapy: after a work injury, the doctor suggests 6 weeks of therapy in Walla Walla, twice a week (copays and gas). Therapy clears it; toughing it out leaves a small, lasting drain on health until you start therapy later (a stop on a Walla Walla trip).

Menu → 📤 Back up or restore: download a backup file or copy a backup code, then on another device use 📥 Restore from a backup (on the title screen or in the same menu). You can add the backup's lives to empty slots or replace all your lives.
Open Menu → ⚙️ Settings (or Settings on the title screen). Settings are saved on this device for every life and never change the game's numbers.
Everything is 60% off at the Kennewick mall.
Early-bird season passes for Bluewood are on sale.
The same old-timer is at the gas station every morning you fill up.
The state safety inspector is coming next week.
A band from Walla Walla is playing The Royal Brick on Saturday night.

Everything you own minus what you owe: cash (below $0 it counts against you), your home equity, your vehicle, your 401(k), index funds at today's value, wine futures at what you paid until they pay out, and what your business would sell for. Then it takes off what's left on a truck loan, student loans and a home equity loan. It counts for 30% of your Life Score.
A new manager starts Monday. Everyone is nervous.
